newsitem.title: USA: ITT SEEN REJECTING HILTON, SWEETENING PLAN.
newsitem.headline: ITT SEEN REJECTING HILTON, SWEETENING PLAN.

text.p: Hotel and casino giant ITT Corp. is expected to flatly reject Hilton Hotels Corp's latest bid and possibly enhance its stock buyback plan in order to thwart a hostile takeover.

Although Hilton's $70 per share offer is far more viable than the $55 bid it launched in January, industry experts said the new price would not bring ITT to the bargaining table and did not represent a knock-out bid.
Instead, the new bid will likely push ITT to build upon a massive restructuring plan announced last month.
"I think they have to be more responsive," said Arthur Adler, a partner in the lodging and gaming advisory group at Coopers & Lybrand.
As part of the company's revamp, ITT launched a plan to buy back up to 26 percent of its stock, or 30 million shares, for $70 each. The $2.1 billion self-tender is set to expire on Aug. 13.
The restructuring also calls for ITT to split the company into three publicly-traded pieces.
Although the plan has won widespread praise on Wall Street, analysts said ITT cannot rest on those laurels.
"This is a real bid and ITT has to have a real response. But there's no way Hilton will get ITT for $70 per share," said James Murren of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Analysts said ITT could raise the self-tender to $75 or $80 per share and buy back a bigger block of stock. Hilton's $70 cash and stock bid is viewed to be at the upper end of what it could pay without diluting earnings.

ITT also could try to enhance shareholder value by selling more assets. Although it has sold a handful of valuable non-core assets, ITT still has properties on the block, including luxury hotels in the U.S. and Europe.
"They've got to find a way to make themselves more valuable than $70 per share," said David Loeb of Credit Lyonnais Securities USA Inc.
In the meantime, the two companies face another court fight in which the victor is likely to assume the final upper hand in the takeover effort.

Hilton on Tuesday filed a lawsuit against ITT seeking to stop its planned restructuring and force a shareholder vote on the proposed break-up of the company. Hilton's latest bid was viewed as critical to support its lawsuit in which it contends that ITT's plans do not create value for shareholders.
ITT had filed a pre-emptive strike in court against Hilton last month, seeking to prohibit it from trying to block the restructuring plan.
"We think Hilton is unlikely to be successful in their bid unless the Nevada court proves to be on their side," said Joyce Minor of Lehman Brothers.
No date has been set yet for a hearing on the issue.
